rotations.name: What you asked for
rotations.why: 4 plots of summer cash crops, as you requested.
rotations.evidence: Estimated soil loss 11.2 t/ha/year on the north slope vs. a tolerance of 7 (RUSLE with IMERG rain and SRTM slope).
rotations.benefits: Highest short-term income in normal years.
rotations.gaps: Exact tolerance depends on the official soil unit (CONEAT); confirm with your agronomist.
rotations.risks: Bare soil for 6 months every winter; in the 2025-26 drought the same pattern lost about a third of its greenness.

rotations.name: Recommended
rotations.why: The north slope erodes easily: keep it under permanent pasture and farm the flatter 72% in 2 plots that never stay bare in winter.
rotations.evidence: Estimated soil loss 4.1 t/ha/year, below the tolerance. Long-term rotation trials at INIA La Estanzuela show rotations with pasture keep more soil carbon.
rotations.benefits: Soil always covered, a grass-legume-grass sequence that breaks pest cycles, and forage for livestock.
rotations.gaps: Cover crop establishment depends on autumn rain; check soil moisture (SMAP) before sowing.
rotations.risks: About 15% less grain income in normal years; needs grazing or a hay buyer for the pasture.

rotations.name: Alternative
rotations.why: Crop-pasture rotation: 3 years of crops, then 3 years of pasture, like the oldest rotation trial in South America.
rotations.evidence: Rotations with pasture had 12-30% more soil carbon than continuous cropping in Uruguayan trials (García Préchac et al., INIA).
rotations.benefits: Best soil protection and drought resilience; strong fit if you keep cattle.
rotations.gaps: Income depends on beef prices and stocking rate, not modeled here.
rotations.risks: Lowest grain income; requires fencing and water for animals.
